title: Adic formal smoothness passes to the completions of source and target
statement: Let $\varphi:(A,\mathfrak m_A)\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local rings, and let $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m_A^n$ and $B^\wedge=\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak m_B^n$ be their completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The maps induced by $\varphi$ define a homomorphism $\varphi^\wedge:A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$. If $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], then $B^\wedge$ is formally smooth over $A^\wedge$ for the $\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$-adic topology.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion), equivalence of (1) and (3), and its proof

proof.text: *Setup: the ideals are finitely generated, and the map $\varphi^\wedge$.* Since $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian, $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$ are finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $\iota_A:A\to A^\wedge$, $\iota_B:B\to B^\wedge$ be the canonical maps [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. As $\varphi$ is local, $\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$, hence $\varphi(\mathfrak m_A^n)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B^n$ for all $n$ (generators $x_1\cdots x_n$ go to $\varphi(x_1)\cdots\varphi(x_n)$), so $\varphi$ induces ring maps $\varphi_n:A/\mathfrak m_A^n\to B/\mathfrak m_B^n$ compatible with the projections [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and $\varphi^\wedge((x_n)_n)=(\varphi_n(x_n))_n$ is a ring map $A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ with $\varphi^\wedge\circ\iota_A=\iota_B\circ\varphi$. We regard $B^\wedge$ as an $A^\wedge$-algebra via $\varphi^\wedge$ and as an $A$-algebra via $\varphi^\wedge\circ\iota_A=\iota_B\circ\varphi$ (the structure of [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-completion] for $R=A$, $S=B$). Moreover $\varphi^\wedge(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)\subseteq\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$: the ideal $\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge$ is generated by the $\iota_A(a)$, $a\in\mathfrak m_A$, and $\varphi^\wedge(\iota_A(a))=\iota_B(\varphi(a))$ with $\varphi(a)\in\mathfrak m_B$; hence $\varphi^\wedge((\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^j)\subseteq(\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge)^j$ for every $j\ge1$ (images of products of generators). (Source: 'Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of topological rings', with continuity of $\varphi$ for the adic topologies, Lemma Tag 07E9.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224), proof (lines 9242-9251); statement of 07ED (homomorphism of topological rings) and Lemma Tag 07E9 (lemma-continuous, line 9025)

proof.text: *(1) $\Rightarrow$ (2): $B^\wedge$ is formally smooth over $A$.* By hypothesis $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], and $\mathfrak m_B$ is finitely generated (step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-completion] (with $R=A$, $S=B$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_B$), $B^\wedge$, an $A$-algebra via $\iota_B\circ\varphi$, is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$-adic topology. (Source: the correspondence of the diagrams for (1) and (2), which uses $B^\wedge/\mathfrak m_B^nB^\wedge=B/\mathfrak m_B^n$, Algebra Lemma Tag 05GG.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224), proof (lines 9242-9251): 'diagrams as in Definition 07EB for the cases (1), (2), and (3) are in 1-to-1 correspondence', (1) and (2)

proof.text: *The lifting problem for $B^\wedge$ over $A^\wedge$; the map $A^\wedge\to D$ kills a power of $\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge$.* By [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] (for $\varphi^\wedge:A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ and the ideal $\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$) let $D$ be a commutative ring with a ring map $h:A^\wedge\to D$, $J\subseteq D$ an ideal with $J^2=0$, $q:D\to D/J$ the quotient map [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and $g:B^\wedge\to D/J$ a homomorphism of $A^\wedge$-algebras, i.e. $g\circ\varphi^\wedge=q\circ h$, with $g((\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge)^k)=0$ for some $k\ge1$. We must find a homomorphism of $A^\wedge$-algebras $f:B^\wedge\to D$ (i.e. $f\circ\varphi^\wedge=h$) with $q\circ f=g$. For $x\in(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^k$ we have $\varphi^\wedge(x)\in(\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge)^k$ (step 1), so $q(h(x))=g(\varphi^\wedge(x))=0$ and $h(x)\in J$. The ideal $(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^{2k}$ is generated by products $xy$ with $x,y\in(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^k$, and $h(xy)=h(x)h(y)\in J^2=0$; so $h((\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^{2k})=0$. (Source: this is the argument of the proof of Lemma 07EC, (2)(a) from (2)(b), lines 9203-9210: '$\mathfrak m^{nk}$ maps into $J$ ... Thus $\mathfrak m^{2nk}$ maps to zero in $A$ and we see that $R\to A$ is continuous'; it shows that $h$ is automatically continuous for the $\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge$-adic topology, so the diagrams of the definition (with $A^\wedge$ discrete) are those of 07ED (3).)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EC (lemma-formally-smooth, line 9165), proof of (2)(b) => (2)(a), lines 9201-9210; used for the case (3) of Lemma Tag 07ED

proof.text: *A lift over $A$.* Regard $D$ as an $A$-algebra via $h\circ\iota_A$ and $D/J$ via $q\circ h\circ\iota_A$. Then $g$ is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras for the structure of $B^\wedge$ through $\iota_B\circ\varphi$: $g\circ\iota_B\circ\varphi=g\circ\varphi^\wedge\circ\iota_A=q\circ h\circ\iota_A$ (step 1, step 3). It kills $(\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge)^k$. By step 2 and [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] (for $B^\wedge$ over $A$ with the ideal $\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$) there is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras $f:B^\wedge\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$; thus $f\circ\iota_B\circ\varphi=h\circ\iota_A$, i.e. $f\circ\varphi^\wedge\circ\iota_A=h\circ\iota_A$. Remark (a) of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], written out: for $y\in(\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge)^k$, $q(f(y))=g(y)=0$, so $f(y)\in J$, and products of two such elements generate $(\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge)^{2k}$ and go to $J^2=0$; so $f((\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge)^{2k})=0$, and by step 1 $f\circ\varphi^\wedge$ kills $(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^{2k}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224), proof (lines 9242-9251): the 1-to-1 correspondence of the diagrams for (2) and (3) (a diagram for (3) restricts along $R\to R^\wedge$ to one for (2)); remark (a) as in the proof of Lemma Tag 07EC (1), lines 9194-9197

proof.text: *$f$ is an $A^\wedge$-algebra map, which proves (3).* By step 1 $\mathfrak m_A$ is finitely generated, so [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] (with $A$, $I=\mathfrak m_A$, $N=2k$) gives $\pi_{2k}:A^\wedge\to A/\mathfrak m_A^{2k}$ surjective with $\pi_{2k}\circ\iota_A$ the quotient map $p_{2k}:A\to A/\mathfrak m_A^{2k}$ and $\ker\pi_{2k}=\mathfrak m_A^{2k}A^\wedge$, the ideal generated by $\iota_A(\mathfrak m_A^{2k})$. This ideal equals $(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^{2k}$: generators $\iota_A(x_1\cdots x_{2k})=\iota_A(x_1)\cdots\iota_A(x_{2k})$ ($x_i\in\mathfrak m_A$) lie in $(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^{2k}$, and conversely a product of $2k$ elements $\sum_l\iota_A(x_{il})s_{il}$ expands into terms $\iota_A(x_{1l_1}\cdots x_{2k\,l_{2k}})s$ in $\mathfrak m_A^{2k}A^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Now let $x\in A^\wedge$; choose $a\in A$ with $p_{2k}(a)=\pi_{2k}(x)$ ($p_{2k}$ is surjective); then $x-\iota_A(a)\in\ker\pi_{2k}=(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^{2k}$. Both $h$ (step 3) and $f\circ\varphi^\wedge$ (step 4) kill $(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^{2k}$ and agree on $\iota_A(a)$ (step 4), so $f(\varphi^\wedge(x))=f(\varphi^\wedge(\iota_A(a)))=h(\iota_A(a))=h(x)$. Hence $f\circ\varphi^\wedge=h$: $f$ is a homomorphism of $A^\wedge$-algebras with $q\circ f=g$. Every lifting problem of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for $B^\wedge$ over $A^\wedge$ with the ideal $\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$ is solved, so $B^\wedge$ is formally smooth over $A^\wedge$ for the $\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$-adic topology. (Source: '$R^\wedge/\mathfrak m^nR^\wedge=R/\mathfrak m^n$, see Algebra, Lemma 05GG ... Thus it is clear that diagrams ... for the cases (1), (2), and (3) are in 1-to-1 correspondence': a continuous map out of $A^\wedge$ into a discrete ring is determined by its restriction to $A$.)
